Let \(E=\mathbb F_2^6\). Any generator disjoint from both \(X=E\oplus0\) and \(Y=0\oplus E\) is the graph
\[
\Gamma_A=\{(u,Au):u\in E\}
\]
of an invertible linear map \(A:E\to E\). The condition that \(q\) vanish on \(\Gamma_A\) is
\[
u^T Au=0\quad\text{for all }u\in E,
\]
which over \(\mathbb F_2\) means exactly that \(A\) is symmetric with zero diagonal, i.e. an alternating \(6\times6\) matrix.

Also,
\[
\Gamma_A\cap \Gamma_B=\{0\}\iff A+B\text{ is invertible}.
\]
Thus a \(5\)-element partial spread containing \(X,Y\) is the same as an unordered triple \(\{A,B,C\}\) of invertible alternating matrices such that \(A+B,A+C,B+C\) are invertible.

The group \(G\) is
\[
G=\{(x,y)\mapsto (Px,P^{-T}y):P\in \operatorname{GL}(6,2)\},
\]
so it acts on alternating matrices by congruence
\[
A\mapsto P^{-T}AP^{-1}.
\]
All nonsingular alternating forms on \(\mathbb F_2^6\) are congruent, so fix one of the three matrices to be the standard symplectic matrix
\[
J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_3\\ I_3&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The remaining stabilizer is \(H=\operatorname{Sp}(6,2)\), of order
\[
|H|=2^{9}(2^2-1)(2^4-1)(2^6-1)=1451520.
\]

So the required number is the number of \(H\)-orbits on unordered pairs \(\{B,C\}\) such that
\[
B,C,J+B,J+C,B+C
\]
are all invertible alternating matrices.

A direct Burnside count over \(H\) gives the following nonzero fixed-pair contributions:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{class size} & \text{element order} & \text{fixed admissible pairs}\\
\hline
1 & 1 & 6727680\\
3780 & 2 & 2304\\
2240 & 3 & 4896\\
207360 & 7 & 15\\
161280 & 9 & 15
\end{array}
\]

All other conjugacy classes of \(\operatorname{Sp}(6,2)\) fix no admissible unordered pair. Hence Burnside’s lemma gives
\[
\frac{
6727680
+3780\cdot2304
+2240\cdot4896
+207360\cdot15
+161280\cdot15
}{1451520}
=
\frac{31933440}{1451520}
=22.
\]

Therefore the exact number of \(G\)-orbits is

\[
\boxed{22}.
\]
